newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-YEBOAH GOING NOWHERE, SAYS GRAHAM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-YEBOAH GOING NOWHERE, SAYS GRAHAM.

text.p: Unsettled Ghanaian striker Tony Yeboah is staying in English soccer, according to new Leeds manager George Graham.
Yeboah has publicly declared his discontent with life at Leeds and claims there has been interest in his services from clubs in Germany and France.
Graham has denied a rift with the player, but has warned the 30-year-old striker about his future conduct.
"Tony has one-and-a-half years of his current contract to run and no-one would be happier than me if he sees it out.
"I told him this morning that if he has problems he should come and see me in my office, not go running to the papers.
"It is all down to frustration because he has been out for so long, The team has put a good little run together and he wants to be part of it.
"We are hoping his latest injury is not too serious and that he will be fit for a run-out in the reserves next week. At least Tony's remarks show he is passionate and hungry."
Yeboah was signed by former manager Howard Wilkinson for 3.4 million pounds from German club Eintracht Frankfurt during the 1994-95 season.
The African's spectacular goals made him so popular he was voted player of the year by Leeds supporters after almost single-handedly securing the club's place in the UEFA Cup.
But he has been out of the side since the 3-0 League Cup final defeat by Aston Villa at Wembley last March and has been suffering from a recurring knee injury.
